statements.venue: Letter to the chief executives of Google and Spirit Airlines, co-signed with other members of Congress
statements.quote: The unprecedented scale and sophistication of modern artificial intelligence make it particularly important that privacy protections keep pace with the technology.
statements.context: Letter opposing the transfer of Spirit Airlines employee data to Google for training AI systems, on worker privacy grounds; Hoyle is one of many signers (led by Rep. Steven Horsford, also signed by Sen. Elizabeth Warren).
statements.reason: The letter is about AI and worker privacy, which is outside the scope of catastrophic risk, so it is level D.

slowdown.note: Original co-sponsor (not her own statement) of H.R. 10538, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026, whose Section 8 puts each advanced AI system under a 'mandatory pause' until a new federal Department of Artificial Intelligence issues rules; a pause for safety reasons counts as yes here.

pause.note: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538; the bill's mandatory pause on advanced AI is conditional on the new department issuing safety rules, which the rubric treats as mixed. No statement of her own found.

intl.note: H.R. 10538 directs pursuit of international agreements to prevent artificial superintelligence but does not name China or talks with China on pacing; nothing else found.

rsi.note: Co-sponsor of H.R. 10538. Its Section 9(a) bans AI systems with 'superintelligence precursor characteristics', defined in Section 3(6)(A) to include 'The capacity to automate or greatly accelerate the process of artificial intelligence research and development', and its mandatory pause covers training 'including through recursive self-improvement'. This reading of the bill text matches other co-sponsors' files; a reviewer should confirm it.

record: Original co-sponsor of H.R. 10538, the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026 (introduced by Rep. Casar), which bans artificial superintelligence and its precursor capabilities, imposes a mandatory pause on advanced AI until a new federal Department of Artificial Intelligence issues rules, and directs pursuit of international agreements to prevent superintelligence.

grade_reason: No statement in her own words about catastrophic AI risk was found since January 2025; her only AI statement found is a 2026 co-signed letter about worker privacy and AI training data (level D). Her record does include original co-sponsorship of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act in September 2026, a strong action on catastrophic risk, so a reviewer may want to grade higher on the record.
